title.narrative: CO- Humanitarian Response in Bari Region

description.narrative:
The project is designed to leverage and complement organizational capacities of both Oxfam and KAALO. Oxfam and KAALO are long-standing partners. Our joint programming is spanning across geographies in Puntland, South-Central Regions and SSC Khatumo areas for humanitarian and long-term programs. Both KAALO and Oxfam are part of Nexus Consortium to promote localization and humanitarian, development and Peace Nexus approach as well as Start Network Supported Somalia Humanitarian Hub with vision to localizethe humanitarian actions – including shifting decision making power and local leadership.
Considering the scale of crisis, urgent unmet needs of displaced population, and the limited capacity of host communities to support IDPs, severe gaps in responsedue to funding availability and operational and programmatic capacities of Oxfam and KAALO, jointly we have prioritized 6 locations with aim to deliver assistance proposed under this project within 45 days. Oxfam and KAALO’s understanding about dynamicand complex context, established working relationships with key stakeholders – including authorities and communities at Puntland, Bari region and proposed districts of Qandala and Iskushuban are enabling factors to ensure timely delivery with expected levelof stakeholder and community engagement and participation. Major assistance proposed under this project that requires procurement is multi-purpose cash transfer, distribution of hygiene kits, and an emergency water supply using cash modality, it is possible to deliver timely as both Oxfam and KAALO have existing framework agreements with multiple suppliers. During project design, stock checks have been done that ensure that suppliers are available locally and can be sourced immediately upon availabilityof the funds.
Qualified and experienced staff of Oxfam and KAALO – including project lead, Protection Officers, Public Health Engineers, Public Health Promoters and Food Security and Cash Officers and MEAL officers are equipped to deliver the assistanceimmediately with the support of logistics, finance, partnerships and safety and security colleagues from Garowe office. Oxfam’s Food Security and Cash, WASH and Protection technical experts, Program Quality Lead and Humanitarian Lead will provide technical oversight and handholding to field-based staff to deliver the proposed assistance andmonitor against the set quality benchmarks – including visits to proposed targeted locations for the response. While the project is45 days, Oxfam and its partnerwill ensure community engagement work takes place in the first week of project approval. this will befollowed by beneficiaries selection and verification process, a task that is at critical juncture and Oxfam understands the importance of ensuring projectreaches the intended beneficiaries. Thus, Oxfam and its partner will lead the entire beneficiaries selection process to ensure zerod diversion of resources in the hands of gate keepers. in two weeks time we aim first cash transfer reaches the beneficairies.
To effectively reach the affected communities within 45 days, the response plan involves a coordinated approach leveraging the efforts of Oxfam and KAALO team to immediately purchase the necessary hygiene kits, contract water truck owners, setup operation of trucking and ensure most vulnerable communities are registered. We will work closely with government representatives and other stakeholders. We will identify and train 10 trained health volunteers who will engage directly with the population.Thesevolunteers will conduct outreach to 10,000 individuals, facilitating not only the distribution of hygiene kits but also promoting hygiene education and practices. By utilizing established community networks and targeting households through organized distributions, we aim to ensure that essential items are delivered promptly. Additionally, the water trucking service will operate concurrently, providing approximately 7.5 liters of clean water per day per person to 1,000 households, thereby addressingimmediate needs while our hygiene promotion efforts help improve overall health and sanitation awareness in the community.
Fifty cases will be supported throughcash-for-protection on a demand basis. Individuals eligible for cash-for-protection mustmeet criteria that include survivors of torture, survivors of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), unaccompanied or separated children, among others. The selection processwill be guided by Oxfam's Cash for Protection Standard Operating Procedures (SOP). The KAALO protection team, along with 12 gender-balanced community protection volunteers, will facilitate the service mapping exercise and protection awareness-raising sessions. A total of 2,050 beneficiaries will be reached through these protectionawareness-raising sessions.
Oxfam and KAALO will actively participate and attend various coordination mechanisms in Bari region and Puntland in general, including the recently established Qandala Area Based Coordination (ABC), Protection, Livelihood, Cashand WASH clusters. Our engagement in these clusters always enable us tocollaborate closely with other key stakeholders and contribute to the collective efforts in addressing protection, Water, Sanitation, Hygiene (WASH), and livelihood challenges.
KAALO and Oxfam have also well established and effective coordination with local communities, local authorities, regional administration, Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (MoHADM), Puntland Water Development Agency (PWDA), Ministry of Planning,and Somalia NGO consortium where both organizations are in the area advisory body which KAALO chairs. These collaboration always help us leverage existing relationships, enhance aid coordination efforts, and ensure the effectiveness of ourinterventions and avoid overlap

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
